snippet.description:
Host and “Loki” star Tom Hiddleston and “Loki” executive producer Kevin R. Wright reunite for Pompeii: Out of Time, a fusion of cinematic scripted drama and investigative documentary storytelling that transports audiences to ancient Rome in the hours before and during the eruption of Mount Vesuvius. Guided by a team of archaeologists, historians, geologists and disaster experts, he uncovers remarkable evidence — and the stories of real people that challenge long-held assumptions about Pompeii and its final hours — not least revealing that many of those caught up in the disaster had the chance to survive. Blending cutting-edge archaeological discoveries, expert analysis and deeply personal storytelling, the series reframes Pompeii not as a story of destruction but as a human drama of resilience, sacrifice and survival, revealing the lives, choices and destinies of those who stood in the shadow of Vesuvius.

snippet.title: This Day in History March 2nd
snippet.description:
March 2nd: A Day of Historical Firsts and Unforgettable Feats!

Journey through time and discover the remarkable events that have made March 2nd a significant date in history! From the birth of American democracy to groundbreaking achievements in sports and space exploration, this day has witnessed it all!

Here's a glimpse of what you'll uncover:

1789: The very first United States Congress meets in New York City, laying the foundation for a nation and setting the stage for American democracy.
1836: Texas declares its independence from Mexico, a bold move that ignited a revolution and led to the establishment of the Lone Star Republic.
1933: "King Kong" premieres in New York City, captivating audiences with its groundbreaking special effects and forever changing the landscape of cinema.
1962: Wilt Chamberlain achieves the unimaginable, scoring an astounding 100 points in a single NBA game, a record that remains unbroken to this day.
1972: NASA launches Pioneer 10, the first spacecraft to venture into the outer planets, paving the way for space exploration and expanding our understanding of the solar system.
1985: Mikhail Gorbachev takes the helm in the Soviet Union, leading to major reforms and ultimately, the end of the Cold War.

Join us as we explore these captivating historical moments and uncover the surprising connections that make March 2nd a day to remember!

snippet.title: They found 28 gold bars in their garden!
snippet.description:
In Roanne, France, a legal dispute unfolded when a couple was instructed by the court to return gold bars unearthed in their garden to the previous owners of their property. Additionally, they were mandated to repay the sum equivalent to the value of the previously sold bars, totaling 642,000 euros, or 693,000 USD. The couple's unexpected discovery, initially comprising six gold bars in 2009 and further expanded to 28 in 2013, triggered a criminal investigation following a report by a government's anti-money laundering organization, concerning irregular financial activities linked to the couple.

Despite the couple's claims of good faith ownership and their reporting of the discovery to relevant authorities, the former owners, represented by the widow of the property's seller and her eight children, contested the couple's rights to the gold bars. The subsequent legal proceedings culminated in a trial at the Roanne High Court in 2014, where the former owners presented evidence supporting their assertion of familial inheritance. Ultimately, the court ruled in favor of the former owners, mandating the return of the remaining five bars and the reimbursement of the proceeds from the sale of the 23 bars, an amount estimated by the Court of Cassation to be around 642,000 euros, following the exhausted legal appeals made by the couple.

Source: https://www.ladepeche.fr/article/2018/06/28/2826770-roanne-couple-contraint-rendre-28-lingots-or-trouves-jardin.html

We use the word "depressed" so casually it's lost all its weight — but real clinical depression is a completely different animal from a bad day. snippet.title: Ireland’s Ancient Moving Stone Door Hid Something No One Was Supposed To See
snippet.description:
Ireland’s Ancient Moving Stone Door Hid Something No One Was Supposed To See

Tourists and park rangers at the Giant’s Causeway in Ireland watched a solid slab of basalt swing open like a door and close again without leaving a single mark. No crack. No dust. No trace it had ever moved. Everyone laughed it off. Rock does not do that. So they called it a hoax and moved on. But one former archaeologist drove to that cliff alone, with no permit and no crew, pressed a drill into the rock beside that door, and sent a camera through the hole. What that camera found inside a sealed chamber that had been closed for longer than anyone can measure will change the way you see that cliff forever.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Explore ancient Egypt’s greatest mysteries in this Lost Treasures of Egypt Season 2 MEGA Episode from National Geographic. Archaeologists investigate the secrets of Tutankhamun, the evolution of Egypt’s pyramids, and the powerful dynasties of pharaohs including Ramses. From hidden tombs and lost chambers to new discoveries along the Red Sea coast and remote desert sites, this compilation uncovers how ancient Egypt’s rulers shaped one of history’s most fascinating civilizations. Featuring three, complete full episodes: 

Tutankhamun’s Unsolved Secrets - 00:00 
Archaeologists are on the trail of Tutankhamun. To piece together his story they search his tomb and beyond for secrets missed by the first explorers. 

Secrets of the Lost Pyramids - 44:01
Archaeologists study the mysterious pyramids that followed the Giza pyramids. They unearth new tombs and chambers to uncover their beguiling story.

Ramses: Egypt's Greatest Dynasty - 01:28:03
Archaeologists piece together how the pyramids evolved. They unearth exciting new evidence, from the spectacular Red Sea coast to the remote desert.

Some secrets don't stay buried — they just wait for the right moment to come out. In this video, we count down 10 things governments quietly admitted years, sometimes decades, later: covert experiments, manufactured wars, secret surveillance, and cover stories built on top of other cover stories.
From the Tuskegee and Guatemala syphilis experiments, to Operation Northwoods, MKUltra, the Gulf of Tonkin, COINTELPRO, Agent Orange, the Roswell weather balloon, and the mass surveillance programs revealed in 2013 — each story follows the same uncomfortable pattern. The truth almost never arrives on time, and almost never arrives voluntarily.
This isn't about paranoia or conspiracy theories. It's about real, documented, declassified history — and what the timing of these admissions reveals about how institutions actually behave.

snippet.title: Which Treasure Would You Chase First?
snippet.description:
Search for: Campfire Creepers: Top Three Hidden Treasures in Pennsylvania to watch complete video.

These three Pennsylvania treasures aren't well known, but will keep you on the edge of you seat. Why more aren't actively looking for them is a surprise.

In this short segment we feature a native American mystery. Long before Indian Caverns became a tourist attraction locals spoke of a sealed chamber hidden deep within the limestone system.
 
The chamber was rumored to contain Native American silver ornaments ritual items carved stone plates trade bars and silver ingots.

 Portions of the cavern were closed decades ago and were never fully surveyed Estimated value: a single 1700s silver trade bar can sell for $5,000 to $30,000 Combined with ritual silver and artifacts the collectable value of a large cache could easily surpass one million dollars.

So which treasure would you chase first Outlaw silver. Prohibition gol, the sunken fortune beneath Lake Wallenpaupack or the Indian Caverns?

snippet.title: Archaeologists Find a Sealed Room in Petra - And What’s Inside Is Horrifying
snippet.description:
Archaeologists Find a Sealed Room in Petra - And What’s Inside Is Horrifying

In 2024, archaeologists in Petra, Jordan broke through stone that had sealed shut for two thousand years. Twelve skeletons lay in a circle, facing each other, exactly as they had been placed the day they died. One skeleton still gripped a small stone cup, holding on even in death. This sealed room sat beneath the Treasury, where more than a million tourists pass every year without knowing what was underneath them. What the team found inside left them asking a far darker question. If this much had stayed hidden for two thousand years, what else is still buried beneath Petra.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
